title: A work order that is never split is credited exactly as before
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Two active staff members at {Location-A} have their "Sales Representative" switch on: {Sales-rep-A} and {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Sales-rep-A} is ZZAUTOTEST Ann Able and {Sales-rep-B} is ZZAUTOTEST Ben Able.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has no sales representative.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST SSR Fleet.
  • {Location-A}'s Shop Supplies Charge is 0%, and nothing else is invoiced at {Location-A} today.
  • Work order {Work-order-1} for {Customer-A} is open and not invoiced; it has one labor line of 2.00 hours at $100.00 an hour and one part with cost $30.00 sold at $50.00; its one Sales Representative reads {Sales-rep-A}.
    For example: {Work-order-1} is S2-40001.
  • Starting screen: {Work-order-1} is open in a desktop browser at least 1024 px wide.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Invoice {Work-order-1}.
  2. Open Reports > Sales By Representative for today with the Sales Type column off.
  3. Turn the Sales Type column on.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the invoice is created.
  • Step 2: {Sales-rep-A} has one row for the invoice with Labor Invoiced $200.00, Parts Invoiced $50.00, Parts Margin $20.00, all figures as before the release.
  • Step 3: the same one row, with Sales Type "Labor, Parts".

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 8 (14 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 19 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative)

  • Feature Overview: “A shop that never adds a field sees one Sales Representative field, as today. The one person is credited with the whole invoice.”
  • S5-R10: “When one person, or Unassigned, holds both the Labor and the Parts side of a work order and the Sales Type filter includes both, the two show as one row whose Sales Type reads "Labor, Parts" and whose figures are the sum of both sides.”
  • Story 5 context note: “* Context note: the report already adds up labor and parts separately on every invoice. This story changes who is credited with each part, not how the money is counted.”
  • Goals: “A shop that never splits sees no visible change.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
